# llutils

<!-- badges: start -->
<!-- badges: end -->

llutils runs `match()`, `%in%`, and regex detection on all your cores. It is written in Rust. `par_match()` and `%par_in%` return exactly what base R does, so they are drop-in replacements. `par_detect()` is `grepl()` with the syntax of Rust's [regex](https://docs.rs/regex/latest/regex/#syntax) crate, which never backtracks.

The gains are largest where base R is slow and the work is bound by CPU: matching text against a large dictionary of terms, and looking up millions of keys.

## Dictionary matching

Which of 100,000 strings mention any of 1,000 terms? A backtracking engine tries each term at each position. `par_detect()` compiles the alternation once, into an automaton that finds all terms in one pass, and splits the strings across threads.

```{r dictionary}
library(llutils)
set.seed(1)

word <- function(n) {
  vapply(seq_len(n), function(i) paste(sample(letters, 8, TRUE), collapse = ""), "")
}
vocabulary <- word(1e4)
x <- paste(
  sample(vocabulary, 1e5, TRUE),
  sample(vocabulary, 1e5, TRUE),
  sample(999, 1e5, TRUE)
)
terms <- sample(vocabulary, 1000)
pattern <- paste(terms, collapse = "|")

hits <- par_detect(x, pattern)
head(x[hits], 3)
mean(hits)

bench::mark(
  base = grepl(pattern, x, perl = TRUE),
  stringi = stringi::stri_detect_regex(x, pattern),
  llutils = par_detect(x, pattern),
  min_iterations = 1
)[, c("expression", "median")]
```

Wrap the alternation in `\b(` and `)\b` to match whole words only. Terms that contain regex metacharacters such as `.` or `(` need a backslash in front of them. For a case-insensitive search, lowercase both the strings and the terms: `(?i)` in front of a large alternation defeats the optimization above, and the same search takes hundreds of times longer.

## Matching

```{r match}
keys <- sample.int(1e8, 1e6)
x <- sample.int(1e8, 1e7, TRUE)

bench::mark(
  base = match(x, keys),
  collapse = collapse::fmatch(x, keys),
  llutils = par_match(x, keys),
  min_iterations = 3, filter_gc = FALSE
)[, c("expression", "median")]
```

`par_match()` handles integer, double, character, Date, and POSIXct vectors, and factors by their levels. Other classes, and inputs below 10,000 elements, go to base `match()`. `x %par_in% table` is `%in%`, and `par_in(x, table, nthreads)` is the same as a function.

Both sides are hashed in parallel, so a join-like lookup of 10 million keys into 10 million others takes 0.1 seconds for integers and 0.2 for strings. The numbers behind the comparison with collapse are in `bench/`.

## Threads

The default is all cores, or the `RAYON_NUM_THREADS` environment variable. Every function takes `nthreads`, and `options(llutils.threads = 2)` sets the default for a session. Inputs too small to keep that many threads busy use fewer.

## Regex syntax

Most patterns mean the same in Rust's regex crate and in PCRE. The differences:

- No backreferences or lookaround. In return, matching time grows only linearly with the string.
- `\d`, `\w`, and `\s` match Unicode by default. Write `[0-9]` or `(?-u:\d)` for ASCII.
- Flags go in the pattern: `(?i)` ignores case.
- `NA` gives `NA`, where `grepl()` gives `FALSE`.

## Installation

When llutils is on CRAN, you will be able to install it as usual:

```{r eval=FALSE}
install.packages("llutils")
```

The development version requires the [Rust toolchain](https://rust-lang.org/tools/install/). When Rust is installed, run:

```{r eval=FALSE}
pak::pak("lhdjung/llutils")
# or devtools::install_github("lhdjung/llutils")
```
